business: breakpoint: The Production Disaster Encyclopedia & HackerTube Canon
target: Software engineers, SREs, systems architects, and engineering students who read Hacker News and build production systems
where: Global / Remote (tech hubs: SF, NYC, Seattle, London, Berlin, Bangalore)

segments.name: Junior Engineer & System Design Interview Candidate

behaviours.name: Lindy Purist
behaviours.how: Ignores tech hype, studies foundational papers, SICP, DDIA, and 10+ year conference talks.

behaviours.name: On-Call Veteran
behaviours.how: Has lived through 3 AM outages; wants deep post-mortems with exact triggers and mitigation formulas.

behaviours.name: Interview & Career Grinder
behaviours.how: Watches conference talks and reads failure cases to crack L5/L6 system design rounds.

behaviours.name: Curator & Sharer
behaviours.how: Builds playlists and shares architecture post-mortems in team Slack channels.

behaviours.name: HN Skimmer
behaviours.how: Clicks interesting HN links; bounces in 5 seconds if there is marketing hero fluff or paywalls.

objections: Is this actually useful or just another bookmarked link I will never open again?
Why should I trust these incident autopsies over the original blog posts?
Is it easy to find specific talks and outages, or is it overwhelming with 6,454 videos?
Can I share a specific incident or talk link with my team so they land directly on it?
Is it clutter-free and fast on mobile?
Is there an account login requirement, or is my library local and private?
Does the simulator actually test realistic distributed systems failure, or is it too basic?
habits: reads Hacker News during morning coffee
studies system design during commute or weekend blocks
runs post-mortems after production incidents at work
watches high-signal engineering conference talks at 1.5x speed
